newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks post 15th record close of 1997.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks post 15th record close of 1997.

text.p: Toronto stocks extended last week's gains for their third straight record close on Monday and 15th of this year, on the back of stronger bank stocks.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's key 300 Composite Index climbed 69.62 points to finish at 6491.13.
Trading was light at 60.3 million shares worth C$872.7 million ($634.2 million). Markets in New York and London were closed for holidays.
The weighty bank sector of Canada's largest equities market gained 2.3 percent ahead of quarterly profit reports starting on Tuesday.

Investors bought Canadian issues on Monday because they looked inexpensive compared to U.S. stocks after Friday when Wall Street posted its 20th record finish of the year, Montreal-based strategist Bill Ram said.
"Overall, what we're doing is a little bit of catch-up with New York," he said.
All of Toronto's 14 sub-groups rose, led by consumer products, banks, conglomerates and media.
Advancing stocks outnumbered decliners 553 to 390, while 306 ended steady.
Analysts expected Canada's big six banks to post record profits for the fourth consecutive quarter, starting with Bank of Montreal and Bank of Nova Scotia on Tuesday.
The Royal Bank of Canada, the nation's largest, led the banks' upward march, gaining 1.65 to 61.70. It was followed by Bank of Nova Scotia, the fourth biggest, which jumped 1.25 to 58.80.
Toronto-based Rex Diamond Mining Corp. dropped 0.70 to 2.85 in active trading, shedding nearly 20 percent of its value.

Beverage and entertainment giant Seagram Company Ltd. saw shares gain 1.10 to 56.30 in moderate turnover following a record-breaking opening weekend for "Jurassic Park" movie sequel "The Lost World". The dinosaur flick was released by Universal Pictures, which is 80 percent-owned by Montreal-based Seagram.
"The Lost World" brought in $90.1 million and broke the previous U.S. Memorial Day weekend opening which was held by action movie "Mission Impossible."
